questions.q: What is the stated purpose of the Design & transition activity?
options: To ensure products and services continually meet stakeholder expectations for quality, cost, and time to market, and move smoothly into live operation
To resolve incidents once a service is already live
To negotiate the price of new supplier contracts
To write the organization's long-term strategic plan
questions.explain: This is Design & transition's purpose exactly as ITIL 4 states it — combining design quality with a smooth move into live use.

questions.q: Why does ITIL 4 treat design and transition as one activity rather than two separate ones?
options: Because transition activities always happen before design activities
Because a well-designed service that fails during rollout delivers no value, and a smooth rollout of a poorly designed service just delivers the wrong thing faster
Because ITIL 4 does not actually define a transition activity
Because design and transition use identical job titles in every organization
questions.explain: The two concerns are inseparable in practice, which is why ITIL 4 bundles them into one value chain activity.

questions.q: Which ITIL 4 practice controls when and how a release actually reaches users?
options: Continual Improvement
Service Level Management
Release Management
Incident Management
questions.explain: Release management is the named practice responsible for controlling the rollout of a release to users.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what commonly causes a sound design to still fail during rollout?
options: The design specification itself was wrong from the start
The service was never actually requested by any stakeholder
Plan never produced any architecture or priorities
Inadequate testing, no rollback plan, missing documentation, or an untrained support team
questions.explain: These are transition failures, not design failures — a design can be entirely sound while the handoff into live use still goes wrong.

questions.q: What does Design & transition hand off once a product or service is specified, tested, and ready to operate?
options: It becomes input to Obtain/build and eventually Deliver & support
It is discarded unless Engage approves it a second time
It skips Obtain/build entirely and goes straight to users with no further activity
It replaces the need for a Change enablement assessment
questions.explain: The specified, tested result flows downstream to Obtain/build for sourcing and then to Deliver & support for day-to-day operation.
